back: A record of each employee’s [[imp:gross pay]], [[imp:deductions]], and [[imp:net pay]] for a pay period.
It tracks mandatory taxes (FIT, SIT, FICA) and voluntary deductions (health insurance, 401(k)).
The register is the source document for payroll accounting and tax reporting.
[[imp:Take‑home pay after all deductions.]]
$$\text{Net Pay} = \text{Gross Pay} - \text{Total Deductions}$$
Total deductions = Mandatory taxes (FIT, SIT, SS, Med) + Voluntary items.
1. [[kw:Social Security]] (OASDI): 6.2% on wages up to an annual cap ($168,600 in 2024).
2. [[kw:Medicare]] (HI): 1.45% on all wages (no cap).
High earners pay an additional 0.9% Medicare surtax above $200,000 (single).

back: $$\text{SS Tax} = \text{Gross Pay} \times 0.062$$
Only the first $168,600 of annual wages are subject to this tax.
Once year‑to‑date (YTD) earnings exceed the cap, no more SS tax is withheld.
$$\text{Medicare Tax} = \text{Gross Pay} \times 0.0145$$
No wage cap – applies to every dollar earned.
Additional 0.9% applies to earnings above $200,000 (single) / $250,000 (married jointly).

A tax on wages levied by most states; rules vary widely.

[[imp:Pre‑tax:]] Health insurance, 401(k) contributions, flexible spending accounts.
[[imp:Post‑tax:]] Roth 401(k), union dues, charitable contributions.
Pre‑tax deductions lower current taxable income; post‑tax do not.

cards.front: How do you calculate [[kw:net pay]] step by step?
back: 1. Subtract pre‑tax deductions from gross → taxable income.
2. Calculate FIT and SIT on taxable income.
3. Calculate FICA (SS + Med) on gross (or taxable for pre‑tax? Note: FICA applies to gross before pre‑tax deductions except Section 125 plans; we'll keep it simple).
4. Net = Gross – (Pre‑tax deductions + FIT + SIT + FICA + Post‑tax deductions).
[[imp:Federal Unemployment Tax Act – an employer‑only tax.]]
Gross rate 6.0% on first $7,000 of each employee's wages.
Credit of up to 5.4% for state unemployment taxes → net rate typically 0.6%.
Funds unemployment benefits; not deducted from employee pay.
[[imp:State Unemployment Tax Act – an employer‑only tax.]]
Rates and wage bases vary by state; often the base is higher than $7,000.
Employers pay both FUTA and SUTA; employees do not contribute.
[[imp:Employer matches employee’s SS and Medicare contributions exactly.]]
If employee pays $153 FICA, employer also pays $153.
Total FICA remitted to the government = $306.
This is part of the employer's payroll tax expense.
